source_read: PDF, online-first version (publisher's cover sheet, then article pp. 1–11; print Substance Use & Misuse 54: 549–559): all pages; Figure 1 (PRISMA flow), Figure 2 (bar chart) and Table 1 checked on pages rendered at 110 dpi; flow-chart arithmetic recomputed; Supplementary Tables S1–S7 not available.

key_findings.note: The flow chart does not add up (see missed); the counts the finding gives are the text's.
Figure 2 bars agree with the percentages in the text (p. 5).
'Attributes' is a fair reading of a relative clause (Discussion, p. 8) tying the excess to the ICD rule; the review's own figures give ICD-10 for only 35% of the Japanese studies (see missed).
36% equals 8 of 22, so the printed share may use a different denominator than the 24 case studies.
The four studies are Yeh 2001, Tomiyama 1990, Sato 1983 and Javadian 2016.
Niemi-Pynttäri reference title on p. 11 as stated.
The Japanese hospital setting is in the reference title (p. 10).

reporting_issues.note: 'In which persistence was impossible by design' overstates the source: the laboratory studies observed none (symptoms resolved within 12 hours to 7 days of the last dose, p. 6) in otherwise healthy volunteers (p. 8). Suggested: 'includes six laboratory studies in volunteers, all with 0% persistence'. The consequence (the headline 25% understates the median of clinical studies by an unknown amount) stands. The same phrase recurs in the interpretation gap ('no possible persistence') and in the claim's GRADE reasoning.

risk_of_bias.note: AMSTAR 2 is right for this design, and critically low confidence follows from at least three critical items not met (2, 7, 9); the domain differences below do not change it.

risk_of_bias_domains.note: AMSTAR 2's 'partial yes' requires every one of: two or more databases, keywords or strategy, and justified publication restrictions. The English-language and published-only limits (p. 3) are not justified, so the item is not met even partly. Overall unchanged.
85% of full texts double-judged with 88% agreement (p. 3); abstract screening appears single.

risk_of_bias_domains.domain: 7. List of excluded studies with justification (critical)
risk_of_bias_domains.note: Figure 1 gives counts by reason only.

risk_of_bias_domains.domain: 8. Included studies described in adequate detail
12. Impact of risk of bias on pooled results
13. Risk of bias accounted for in interpretation (critical)
risk_of_bias_domains.note: Arguable: for non-randomized studies AMSTAR 2 accepts a discussion of the likely impact of bias, and the limitations (p. 8) do discuss the direction of design-level biases (institutionalized male samples overstating negative and understating affective symptoms; laboratory confinement inflating hostility and anxiety). Without any study-level assessment, 'no' is the safer reading.

interpretation_gap.note: Minor agreed. Besides the points recorded, the abstract's 'negative symptoms were mostly absent (<20%)' reads as a share of people, while it is a share of studies. The phrase 'no possible persistence' should become 'no persistence observed' (reporting issue 4).

missed: The diagnostic explanation of the Japanese excess is weakly supported by the review's own figures: the discussion says the Japanese studies typically used the ICD (p. 8), but the results give ICD-10 for 35% and DSM-IV for 25% of them (p. 6), so the explanation could apply to about a third of the Japanese studies, and persistence by classification system is not reported. A claim should not say the Japanese studies mostly used ICD-10.

Flow-chart arithmetic (Figure 1, p. 3): 4455 records minus 2043 duplicates is 2412, while the figure gives 2465 abstracts screened and the text 2464; 404 full texts minus 94 included is 310, while the figure gives 303 full-text exclusions, whose reasons sum to 356 because some articles carry several. The search yield cannot be reconstructed.

Case-report denominators mix studies and people: 29 case reports describe 49 cases (p. 4), while duration is given for 'twenty-four case studies' with persistence in two 'participants' (p. 6), and 36% fits 8 of 22. The 8% figure is best cited as 2 of 24 case reports with duration data.
